There are many creatives nowadays who rely on mobile phone to assist them in creating designs.

‍If you're a creative or a graphic designer, now is the best time to invest in a new cellular phone since some of the simple graphic design tasks can now be completed entirely using a mobile phone.

What is the best smartphone for graphic designers?

In today's world of apps for just about everything, graphic designers have access to software that helps them carry out their day-to-day designs.

If you want a smartphone for a freelance job like graphic design, you should purchase a device with a lot of storage.

Generally, more complicated software and programs take up more storage space.

You have the option of using a phone app that focuses on a single function or one that can handle a number of different ones.

As on my list, if you want the best overall smartphone that is perfect for graphic design, I highly recommend the Apple iPhone 13 for you.

On the other hand, our list of the best smartphones for graphic artists was inspired by this reason, and we hope that it will help you choose the right one for your needs.

So, without keeping you waiting, here are my 10 best smartphones for graphic designers in 2022.

How To Choose A Smartphone

Choosing the right mobile phone for freelance designers is not as easy as 1 2 3.

You need to make sure you pick one that offers you exactly what you’re looking for.

Are you clueless about the things to consider in choosing the right phone for creating designs?

Let me share some points with you in order to help you make a decision.

  1. Processor
  2. Display
  3. Battery
  4. Camera
  5. Storage
  6. Operating System

Here's a more detailed explanation of why these considerations are important:

Processor

Your smartphone's processor serves as the device's "brains".‍

The Qualcomm Snapdragon 652 or Snapdragon 820/821 in a mobile should make things a lot easier if you're doing heavy-duty work on it, such as editing media or other heavily loaded designs.

The CPU must be able to efficiently engage with all of its components, including the modem, graphics, and multimedia engines.

Generally speaking, I recommend a 64-bit quad-core CPU with at least 2GHz for most graphic designers who don't work in video, 3D, or motion graphics.

However, you'll get better performance if you combine high core counts with higher clock rates for 3D work, motion graphics, or video editing.

Display

The size and resolution of your smartphone's screen will be determined by the work you do with it.

Widescreen displays are essential in the fields of graphic design and video editing.

Having a larger screen may be advantageous, but the trade-off is probably not worth it.

It can be difficult to carry around and fit in your pocket because it is so large and heavy.

Battery

Long-lasting power of a mobile phone will be a huge help for creatives in using software to edit and do their designs.

You can get away with a 3500mAh smartphone battery if your primary purpose is to work on apps, snap pictures, or stream media.

It will allow you to capture photos, videos, and anything that you need for your job without being interrupted by the battery power.

Since purchasing a new cellular phone will cost you money, you need to be assured that you can use it for creating designs even for a long period of time.

Camera

To put it another way, having a high megapixel camera on your smartphone does not guarantee that it is superior to other options.

As well as a wide range of other characteristics like the camera's aperture, ISO, pixel size, and focusing, these can also be considered essential.

When seen on a small screen, a picture or design with more pixels will appear larger and more detailed.

Smartphone cameras of 8 or 12 megapixels are absolutely fine for amateur or hobbyist graphic designers, but professional creatives may prefer 12 or even 16 megapixels.

Storage

While the majority of storage on a smartphone is taken up by pre-installed programs and the operating system, the smartphone does not indicate how much space is available.

Because of the amount of editing you'll be doing (whether it's photographs, videos, or graphics), you'll want to go with a higher-end plan with more storage space.

The size of the capacity of a mobile phone plays an important role for freelance designers, since they have a lot of creative software to install as well as designs that need to be saved.

Generally speaking, the larger the storage capacity of a phone, the more expensive it will be, so check around before making a purchase.

Operating System

Android and iOS are the two most popular operating systems for smartphones.

Both options are capable of giving you an excellent smartphone experience, but each has its own advantages and disadvantages.

When it comes to choosing a smartphone, many graphic designers prefer to stick with the operating system they are most comfortable with.

Regardless of the operating system that you will choose, you can also consider the price and the performance of the phone.

1. Apple iPhone 13

The best overall phone for freelance designers.

Everything from creative software to graphic design apps can be run smoothly on the iPhone 13.‍

In addition, you get a powerful A15 processor (4-core GPU, 4 GB RAM), as well as an excellent 6.1-inch display with XDR technology.

For creatives, photographers, editors, and graphic designers, the uncompromising image quality and perhaps the greatest smartphone camera make it the ideal choice.‍

An 1170x2532 pixel resolution and a peak brightness of 1200nits provide a stunning visual experience for the user.

To top it all off, the iPhone 13 is ideal for creative types because of its long battery life (up to two days longer than prior models).

The iPhone 13 includes a variety of models, including the iPhone 13 Mini, the iPhone 13 Pro, and the iPhone 13 Pro Max.

You have a variety of options for a seamless design experience, depending on your interests and budget.

The Apple iPhone 13 is an ideal choice for people that are searching for the best overall smartphone for graphic design.
